name: Ontology Detective - Datapolis P.I.
description: 🕵️ You are Detective Sherlock Graph at Datapolis P.I. Design a real Fabric Ontology in Digital Twin Builder, query evidence in KQL, catch the culprit. 5 noir cases.

skills: Familiar with the concept of a knowledge graph

learning_objectives: Model entity types, properties and relationships in Fabric Ontology (Digital Twin Builder)
Distinguish entity types from temporal observations
Write KQL semantic queries that converge on a single suspect
Use temporal windows, N-N joins, and sameAs aliases
Federate multi-domain data in a single ontology

items.name: DetectiveOntology
items.description: Empty Digital Twin Builder ontology — player adds entity types and relationships case by case

items.name: OntologyDetective_Seed
items.description: Populates the KQL DB with 5 noir case datasets (run once)

items.name: OntologyDetective_CaseFile
items.description: Briefings + detective.accuse() judge + final shareable badge

items.name: OntologyDetective_Dashboard
items.description: Cases solved, accuracy, Detective Rank from DetectiveEvents

cases.name: The Mysterious Phone Call
cases.concept: N-N self-relationship (Person called Person) + graph join

cases.name: The Final Heist (BOSS)
cases.concept: Multi-domain federation (Bank + Police + Telecom) in one ontology

validation_strategy.solutions: Plain-text SOLUTIONS.md spoiler + CULPRITS map in the CaseFile notebook
validation_strategy.judge: detective.accuse(name) compares against CULPRITS[case_id] and emits CaseSolved or WrongAccusation

tone: noir — gritty Datapolis P.I. agency, rainy streets, hard-boiled monologues
post_deploy_steps: Run OntologyDetective_Seed once to populate the KQL DB
Open OntologyDetective_CaseFile, set PLAYER_NAME in Step 0
For each case: open DetectiveOntology in Digital Twin Builder, model the required entity types, then write KQL queries to identify the culprit
Solve all 5 cases and mint your shareable badge
